title: Wolves
synopsis: Two fixers, one body, one Manhattan night. Neither of you was supposed to be assigned to this job. Now you're both here, and the clock is small and meaningless and beautiful.

nodes.text: The body is exactly where the call described. So is the second fixer — a man named Park you have heard about but never met. You both stare. “Refuse to share the job” opens the route to The Two Bosses. “Accept the buddy and split it” changes the terms and carries you toward First Move.

choices.text: Refuse to share the job
choices.consequence: Be territorial; survive. You commit to refuse to share the job. It carries you into The Two Bosses while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Accept the buddy and split it
choices.consequence: You choose to accept the buddy and split it. By First Move, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Park, on his burner, calls his guy. You call yours. Both bosses say, 'Do the job.' Neither will admit to the double-dispatch. You and Park look at each other in the elevator mirror. Choose “Make a temporary alliance with Park” and The Doorman comes into view; choose “Pretend to and watch his hands” and the road bends toward Pamela the Hostess.

choices.text: Make a temporary alliance with Park
choices.consequence: Mutual interest, no friendship. You choose to make a temporary alliance with Park. By The Doorman, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Pretend to and watch his hands
choices.consequence: You choose to pretend to and watch his hands. By Pamela the Hostess, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Park is, you discover, oddly funny — dry as a stone, terrified of yellow taxis, allergic to dogs. He compares spread sheets of corpses he has moved in his career. You realize you have just made a friend, which is the worst.

choices.text: Lean into the partnership
choices.consequence: Two heads, fewer mistakes. You lean into the partnership. The way toward The Doorman opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Stay professional, distance everything
choices.consequence: Friendship in this job ends in funerals. You commit to stay professional, distance everything. It carries you into Pamela the Hostess while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: The doorman of the building is alert, awake, and named Mickey. He has seen you both. He is also, suspiciously, willing to be helpful in ways that do not require a tip. The paths divide here: “Bribe Mickey for the camera tape” leads into The Van, while “Walk Mickey through a story he'll repeat” makes Park's Daughter the next reckoning.

choices.consequence: You bribe Mickey for the camera tape. The way toward The Van opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: The penthouse owner — Pamela — returns home unexpectedly. She walks in with grocery bags and a face that has done this once before. 'Again?' she sighs. “Recruit Pamela to help” opens the route to The Van. “Sedate Pamela politely” changes the terms and carries you toward Park's Daughter.

choices.consequence: You commit to recruit Pamela to help. It carries you into The Van while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Sedate Pamela politely
choices.consequence: She'll thank you tomorrow. You commit to sedate Pamela politely. It carries you into Park's Daughter while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Park has a van. You have a freight elevator code. Mickey conveniently looks the other way as you wheel out a 'rolled-up rug.' It is 3:14 a.m. and Manhattan is the wrong city to do this in.

choices.text: Drive to the Hudson
choices.consequence: You choose to drive to the Hudson. By The Cop, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

choices.text: Drive to a friend's freezer truck in the meatpacking district
choices.consequence: You drive to a friend's freezer truck in the meatpacking district. The way toward The Dog Walker opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Park's phone rings — his daughter, 17, can't sleep. He puts her on speaker, casually, while you are mid-cleanup. You realize you have never heard a fixer be a father. The distance between The Cop and The Dog Walker begins with the choice between “Stay quiet while he parents” and “Take over the floor work so he can take the call properly.”

nodes.text: A traffic stop. The officer is twenty-three, bored, and decent. Park makes small talk in fluent New Jersey. You hand over a registration that, on paper, will check out. Probably. “Talk your way past” draws you toward The Boss, Lying; “Pay the cop a bribe respectfully” leaves The Hostess, Again waiting on the other side.

nodes.text: A man with three dachshunds walks past the van. He looks too long. Park, who is allergic, sneezes and the door swings. The distance between The Boss, Lying and The Hostess, Again begins with the choice between “Befriend the dog walker quickly” and “Drive away before he processes.”

choices.text: Befriend the dog walker quickly
choices.consequence: Disarm with social warmth. You commit to befriend the dog walker quickly. It carries you into The Boss, Lying while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Your boss calls again. He admits — finally — that the double-dispatch was on purpose. One of you was supposed to take care of the other one, after. To choose “Tell Park immediately” means meeting The Diner; “Plan to flip on your boss without telling Park” sends you toward The Tunnel instead.

choices.consequence: You choose to tell Park immediately. By The Diner, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: Pamela calls — calmly, after the fact — and offers you both a deal. She has been collecting evidence on the man who employed her to host these meetings. She is, in a real sense, your way out.

choices.text: Take Pamela's deal
choices.consequence: Sometimes a hostess is the boss. You take Pamela's deal. The way toward The Diner opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

choices.text: Refuse and disappear
choices.consequence: You commit to refuse and disappear. It carries you into The Tunnel while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: 5:11 a.m. A diner that smells like every diner you have ever loved. You and Park, both alive, both a little soot-stained, both eating eggs. The waitress refills your coffee without asking. Choose “Plan the rest of the night together” and The Setup comes into view; choose “Eat in companionable silence” and the road bends toward The Trip West.

nodes.text: You drive into the Lincoln Tunnel alone. The boss texts. You don't open it. The yellow lights blur. You become, briefly, a person who is choosing his own next sentence. The paths divide here: “Drive to your sister's house in Queens” leads into The Setup, while “Drive west, indefinitely” makes The Trip West the next reckoning.

nodes.text: You and Park spring the trap on your bosses — together. Pamela helps. Mickey helps. The dog walker is, hilariously, a retired federal agent who helps too. The morning ends with two bosses in custody and a story nobody will believe.

choices.text: Take the deal the feds offer
choices.consequence: Witness protection beats your benefits. You commit to take the deal the feds offer. It carries you into Witness Protection while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Refuse the deal; vanish on your own terms
choices.consequence: Self-reliance to the end. You commit to refuse the deal; vanish on your own terms. It carries you into The Cabin while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

nodes.text: Somewhere in Pennsylvania you stop for coffee at a roadside place. A waitress smiles at you and you realize you are, possibly, allowed to start over. The Hardware Store comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Stay in this town for a season” and “Keep driving until you find the right town.”

choices.text: Keep driving until you find the right town
choices.consequence: You keep driving until you find the right town. The way toward The Hardware Store opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: They give you a new name in a quiet city. You and Park, somehow, get adjacent towns. You meet on Tuesdays in a diner halfway between for eggs and coffee and the pretense of normal lives.

choices.text: Live the small life
choices.consequence: Survival is its own win. You commit to live the small life. It carries you into The Diner Booth while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Discreetly help people who need fixers, ethically
choices.consequence: Even a small life can serve. You discreetly help people who need fixers, ethically. The way toward The Diner Booth opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: You and Park, off-grid, buy a cabin you have no business owning. He fixes the roof. You teach yourself to make bread. The dog walker visits sometimes. Pamela sends Christmas cards. Mickey, baffling, sends Easter cards only.

choices.text: Stay until you grow old
choices.consequence: Some endings are also addresses. You commit to stay until you grow old. It carries you into Late Summer at the Cabin while the safer possibility closes without making a sound.

choices.text: Go out once more for one good cause
choices.consequence: You choose to go out once more for one good cause. By Late Summer at the Cabin, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: You wander into a small-town hardware store that's hiring. The owner is older than the store. You realize that whatever happens next, your hands still know how to make things work. To choose “Take the job here, name on a paycheck” means meeting Roadside Town; “Keep moving — somewhere is still ahead” sends you toward Indefinite instead.

nodes.text: Park slides into the booth with a folded newspaper and the calm of a man who has, against all odds, achieved Tuesday. You decide together what 'normal' means this week. To choose “Just be normal — eggs, paper, no work” means meeting Diner Tuesdays; “Whisper about a case you could quietly help on” sends you toward Quiet Fixers instead.

choices.consequence: Old habits, used kindly. You whisper about a case you could quietly help on. The way toward Quiet Fixers opens, and something on the other side seems to notice.

nodes.text: Bees in the lavender. Park reading on the porch. A phone you almost never use. You realize the only debt you have left is to yourself — and even that, almost paid. The paths divide here: “Stay; this is the ending you chose” leads into The Cabin, while “Take one careful last call — only if it's clean” makes One More Time the next reckoning.

choices.consequence: You choose to take one careful last call — only if it's clean. By One More Time, the danger will know a little more about you than you know about it.

nodes.text: You stay in the small town and become, eventually, a person who fixes things that aren't bodies. Doors, furnaces, the school's drainage. The town accepts you the way small towns do — slowly, then completely. The road into Roadside Town began with “Take the job here, name on a paycheck” in The Hardware Store; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You drive for two years. You read every diner menu in America. You become the kind of person who knows when a town will fit and when it won't. One spring you stop. The town is fine. You are fine. The road, finally, lets you.

Park's daughter graduates. He cries into his coffee. You toast with cheap mugs. You are not, by any government's definition, alive. You have, perhaps for the first time, a life. The road into Diner Tuesdays began with “Just be normal — eggs, paper, no work” in The Diner Booth; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You and Park become the quiet help — for women leaving bad marriages, for whistleblowers needing rides, for a witness needing a Wednesday. You do not call it justice. You call it the work. The road into Quiet Fixers began with “Whisper about a case you could quietly help on” in The Diner Booth; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

Two old fixers, a wood stove, a dog Park finally tolerates. You both live longer than your old boss would have predicted. You are, against every actuarial table, content. The road into The Cabin began with “Stay; this is the ending you chose” in Late Summer at the Cabin; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You go back once, for a thing that needed doing. Park drives. You sit. The job ends cleanly. You return to the cabin a little tired and entirely yourselves. There is no next time. Both of you know it. Both of you are okay.
